acceptance.given: A Skill package declares examples with typical, boundary, and error outcome IDs, and the authoring standard plus examples checker are available for inspection.

oracle.expected: The standard and checker define the three outcome IDs and require additional conditional workflow or child-dispatch evidence before classifying a Skill as an orchestrator.
forbidden: Classifying a leaf Skill as an orchestrator solely because it has the three outcome IDs.
oracle.observable: The standard document and examples-checking implementation contain an artifact-level rule and test assertion distinguishing outcome identification from orchestrator classification.

acceptance.then: A focused artifact and behavior check can identify the declared outcome IDs and independently verify that orchestrator classification requires routing evidence beyond those IDs.
acceptance.when: During validation of the authoring standard and examples checker, inspect the published standard/checker artifacts and execute the bounded examples test selector.

failure_intents.selector_intent: scripts/sc/tests/test_skill_quality_examples.py::test_a06 must fail when the standard or checker treats the presence of typical, boundary, and error outcome IDs as sufficient evidence of orchestrator status.

affected_subjects: Example outcome IDs and orchestrator classification
slice_hint.behavior_change: Define and validate the distinction between example outcome identification and orchestrator classification, requiring routing workflow or child-dispatch evidence for the latter.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Documentation and bounded static-check behavior only; no persisted state or schema migration.

slice_hint.state_transition: Unspecified authoring/classification rules become explicit artifact and checker rules distinguishing outcome IDs from routing capability.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The focused examples test and the whole Package A terminal selection verify the distinction using the real checker artifacts and no orchestrator classification is based solely on the three IDs.
